name: Closed Iniencephaly

criteria.description: Fixed retroflexion of the head with hyperextension of the cervical spine
Defect or absence of the occipital bone leading to a large foramen magnum
Fusion and malformation of cervical vertebrae causing a shortened neck
No open neural tube defect or exposed neural tissue (closed defect)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fixed retroflexion of the head with cervical spine hyperextension, occipital bone defect, and cervical spine malformation without open neural tube exposure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; differentiation from open iniencephaly is critical.

common.symptomName: Shortened neck due to cervical vertebral fusion

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress secondary to thoracic deformity

rare.symptomName: Seizures secondary to associated brain malformations
searchTerms: epilepsy linked to brain structural defects

imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing fixed retroflexion of fetal head
MRI or CT demonstrating occipital bone defect and cervical vertebral fusion
Absence of open neural tube defect on imaging
genetic: No specific gene identified; likely multifactorial etiology with possible neural tube defect gene involvement
other: Prenatal diagnosis possible via detailed fetal imaging
Differentiation from open iniencephaly and anencephaly critical

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of open neural tube defect with exposed neural tissue
Absence of major portions of the brain and skull

redFlags: Fixed retroflexion of the head with cervical hyperextension
Large occipital bone defect with abnormal foramen magnum
Respiratory distress in neonate due to thoracic deformity
